name: jq
summary: Current upstream jq CLI compiled for browser WebAssembly with an isolated Worker/MEMFS runtime and exact source pins.

profiles.label: Browser Full
features: JSON filters, pipes, map/select/reduce and streaming-oriented CLI flags
Oniguruma 6.9.10 regular expressions from the exact jq submodule pin
module/data file loading through Emscripten MEMFS
profiles.output: Generic upstream jq CLI for local JSON filtering and transformation
profiles.size: Loaded from the published release manifest

integration.summary: Self-host jq-core.js/jq-core.wasm plus the Zoo wrapper, then execute normal jq CLI arguments against JSON files staged in MEMFS.
integration.example:
<script src="/vendor/jq/browser-jq.js"></script>
<script type="module">
const jq = WasmZooJq.loadHosted({ baseUrl: "/vendor/jq/" });
try {
  const input = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ users: [{ name: "A", active: true }] }));
  const result = await jq.exec(["-c", ".users | map(select(.active)) | map(.name)", "/input.json"], {
    files: [{ name: "/input.json", data: input }]
  });
  console.log(result.stdout);
} finally {
  jq.dispose();
}
</script>
notes: No SharedArrayBuffer or cross-origin isolation is required for browser-full.
The wrapper preserves jq's CLI argument model and adds only MEMFS file staging plus stdout/stderr capture.
Native terminal/pipe semantics and host filesystem access are not available; files must be staged into MEMFS.

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Current jq CLI with normal host stdin/stdout/filesystem and OS process integration.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Current upstream jq CLI with builtin Oniguruma, isolated Worker execution and browser MEMFS constraints.

notes: jq 1.8.2 is pinned to exact commit 34f7186b86743a083a589741b6cea95293524108; the matching upstream Oniguruma submodule is pinned to 4ef89209a239c1aea328cf13c05a2807e5c146d1 (6.9.10).
The representative jq-web 0.6.2 browser package currently pins jq 1.7.1, while this Zoo profile tracks jq 1.8.2 and uses Emscripten 6.0.7.
The Chromium smoke test verifies jq --version, a real JSON select/map transformation, and an Oniguruma-backed test() regular expression.
jq 1.8.2 includes upstream security fixes released after 1.8.1; WASM Zoo still treats browser execution as untrusted-input processing and isolates each CLI invocation in a fresh Worker.

referenceWasm.name: jq-web
referenceWasm.note: jq-web 0.6.2 uses jq submodule commit 71c2ab509a8628dbbad4bc7b3f98a64aa90d3297, which is jq 1.7.1, and documents Emscripten 3.1.31 as the known-working build version.

capabilityMatrix.feature: jq filter language and upstream CLI
capabilityMatrix.note: The browser artifact builds the upstream jq executable rather than reimplementing the query language in JavaScript.
Built from jq's exact pinned Oniguruma 6.9.10 submodule and exercised by the browser smoke test.
Files can be staged into MEMFS and addressed by ordinary jq CLI paths/options.
The browser wrapper captures stdout/stderr and stages input files; native shell pipe/TTY semantics are not present.
Browser execution is intentionally limited to Emscripten MEMFS.
jq itself has no network client in this profile and the Worker exposes no Zoo network API.
jq browser-full is single-threaded and does not need cross-origin isolation.
